behavior: A text control of the server HTML keeps a value that it gets before the page hydrates: typed text or an autofill. After the hydration, the part handles that value as one `input` event. `Autocomplete.Root` then emits `valueChange` and `update:modelValue`, and `Combobox.Root` emits `inputValueChange` and `update:inputValue`. An `input` listener on `Toolbar.Input` gets the event. One tick later, a changed control that does not have the focus gets `change`, `blur` and `focusout`, as a control that the user left. Its field is then touched, and a validation on blur runs. A control that nobody changed gets no event. With React 19.3, Base UI keeps the text in the DOM and calls no change callback. The state then keeps the value of the server, and the next update of a controlled input writes that value again. The experimental channel of React sends `input` and `change`, and no focus event.
